messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: VeloxPay discovery — cost drivers & next steps

Hi Lina / Tom,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to meet both of you. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed set of next steps so we keep momentum.

Key pain points you described:
- Token spike on peak settlement flows (midnight batch) causing 5-10x day-over-day spend on high-concurrency windows.
- Long tail of long-context LLM tests (user + audit history) that increases avg tokens per request and KV cache miss rate.
- Tight FY27 pilot cap: finance allocated ~$45k for the POC; any overrun will need executive re-approval.

Goals you asked us to help with:
1) Demonstrate a TCO path to hit 50% token-cost reduction for inference (through batching + prefix caching + model variant selection) without degrading user-facing latency beyond 300ms p95.
2) Validate a pilot at 50k monthly active users with realistic peak QPS and 30–60s context windows.
3) Produce a clear pilot SOW and expected savings matrix finance can sign off on.

Immediate observations / recommended levers (high level):
- Batching: continuous batching on settlement window can amortize decoder cost by ~2.5–3x for your QPS pattern.
- Prefix/KV caching: enabling prefix caching for repeated audit-history prefixes should cut tokens by ~15–25% on reads.
- Model routing: mix of 7B quantized for low-latency routings and 13B fp16 for high-quality settling jobs where latency slack exists.

Attachments I added: VeloxPay token econ sheet (simple per-token model with batching scenarios) + draft pilot scope v0.3 (short SOW).

Proposed next steps (pick dates that work):
- Wed 8/4: 30m technical sync with Rishi to validate peak QPS and confirm KV/cache patterns (we can run a micro-benchmark after).
- Fri 8/6: Deliver a pilot TCO slide + 2 scenario options (Conservative / Aggressive) for your finance review.
- Mon 8/9: Sign-off check — confirm pilot budget and go/no-go.

Can you confirm Tom which peak window metrics we should use (QPS distribution + 95th pct token length)? Lina — is the $45k cap a hard limit for PoC or is there wiggle room for a one-time top-up if we show >60% projected saving?

Thanks — I’ve cc’d Marissa to help with SOW and onboarding logistics.

Best,
Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Peak window: our settlement run starts at 00:30 PST and runs ~90m. Peak QPS ~420 sustained for ~12 minutes, tails off to ~45 QPS. We can share a short CSV of 1 week of QPS by minute.
- Token distribution: median request is ~420 tokens, 95th is ~3.2k, but the 99th is where things get expensive (~8–12k) because of full audit dumps. For pilot sizing assume 95th = 3.2k.
- Budget: $45k is what procurement approved for the pilot — finance may approve a one-time top-up if we can show a clear payback in <90 days, but that's not guaranteed.

Two asks:
1) Can you produce a conservative scenario that assumes 0% reduction on the 99th percentile (we can’t change audit dump size), and optimizes everything else?
2) Tom will follow up with the QPS CSV and a short redacted sample of request contexts for caching analysis.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—
Lina Gomez
Head of Platform

Hi Lina / Tom — quick technical note ahead of the sync.

Thanks for sharing the 95th/99th numbers (Ben — appreciate the forward). Two short points that will shape the bench and the conservative scenario: 

1) Batching geometry: given a 12-minute sustained peak at ~420 QPS, continuous batching with a 30–60ms coalescing window should give very high batching efficiency without materially impacting per-request latency for user flows. For the settlement jobs where latency tolerance is higher, we can increase batch window to maximize throughput.

2) Caching and audit dumps: audit dumps will remain expensive; we will exclude 99th requests from caching unless you can provide a deterministic prefix pattern. For the other 95% of requests, enabling prefix/KV caching plus a 2-tier model routing (quantized smaller model for short contexts + fp16 for long contexts) should reduce token spend by ~35% in the conservative scenario and up to ~55% in the aggressive scenario.

I’ll prepare a short micro-bench script and sample config (batch windows, cache TTLs, routing thresholds) for Wed/Thu. Bring the CSV and 10 redacted examples; we’ll run a quick mapping to cache-hit likelihoods before the bench.

Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
